comment: A press on the canvas that closes a top menu, the last title's list or the Welcome window closes it and paints nothing. A painter expects that a click out of a dialog such as a submenu or the Welcome window paints nothing. The dump's open_menus names what is open, history.steps and history.version say whether a stroke landed, and windows says whether the Welcome window and the Brush Presets docker are up.
Every docker parked at the right edge, so each press lands on the document and not on a docker.
02, a press on the document, a drag and a release: Filter closes and no stroke lands.
03, the same press and drag with nothing open paints, one stroke and one step.
04, Edit open and a right press on the canvas: Edit closes and the Brush Presets docker stays parked at the right edge, where before the press brought it to the pointer beside the list.
05, the Welcome window up, opened from Help.
06, a press on the document beside it, a drag and a release: the window goes away and no stroke lands.
07, the Welcome window up again and a press on File: the window goes away and File opens, one press doing both.

08, the Toolbox over the canvas, the Welcome window up and a press on the Eyedropper's button: the window goes away and the press goes on to the docker, which picks the Eyedropper. B takes the brush back.
09, 1280 by 1024 at scale 2, where the last title holds Filter, Modules and Help: its list open, and a press on the document, at a point in logical units, closes it and paints nothing.
11, with each window its own, the Welcome window up and a press on the main window's canvas: it goes away and paints nothing.

13, still with each window its own, Filter open as a window of the OS's own and a press on the canvas, a drag and a release: Filter closes and no stroke lands. The harness hands the press to the main window without the change of focus the OS makes on a real desktop.
